application_gpu_memory.scope: Application VkDeviceMemory: native suballocator blocks including free space, plus dedicated allocations. Excludes driver-internal allocations and swapchain memory. Sampled at graph submission and frame completion.

cold_start.scope: First up to 300 presented frames, independent of warmup and steady samples. Initialization/prewarm and first-present delay are separate top-level measurements. Framework percentiles use each frame's compile+record+submit sum.

performance.scope: CPU wall time. Graph framework is compile+record+submit; framework_including_declarations also includes graph building and begin_frame. Frame protocol also includes acquire/present/display recording; completion wait and CPU reference are separate. GPU values are sums of command timestamp spans per physical queue; spans can overlap and exclude idle gaps, display work and WSI. Their sum is not frame latency, GPU active time, or pure vsync latency. Missing GPU measurements remain absent.

transient.committed_scope: Resource ranges and dedicated backings only; excludes retained suballocator block slack. See application_gpu_memory for actual native reservations.

memory_budget_usage.scope: Known resource ranges/backings and reserved CPU arenas/compiler payload bounds; excludes suballocator block slack, unregistered CPU containers and opaque driver allocations. Native reservations are reported separately.

teardown_memory.scope: Registered resource ranges and budgeted CPU storage after Lab/device owners drop; excludes opaque driver and operating-system allocations.

limitations: Production FrameLoop submits the offscreen graph and display work with timeline dependencies
Per-frame CPU fixture generation and GPU readback are correctness checks, not renderer benchmarks
Production presentation requires maintenance1 and waits actual presentation fences at shutdown
GPU command timestamps require --gpu-timing on; opaque driver pool/pipeline memory is unavailable
